We adopt the following metrics for automatic evaluation: (1) BLEU (B-n)... (2) BERTScore-F1 (BS)... (3) Repetition (R-n)... (4) Distinct (D-n)... For MO2ST we also adopt Coverage (Cov) and Order (Ord).

For generation tasks, we do not use perplexity since perplexity scores are not comparable among models with different vocabularies. We adopt the following metrics for automatic evaluation: (1) BLEU (B-n): It is used to measure n-gram overlaps (n = 1, 2) between generated and ground-truth texts. (2) BERTScore-F1 (BS): It is used to measure the semantic similarity between generated and ground-truth texts. (3) Repetition (R-n): It calculates the ratio of texts that repeat at least one n-gram in all generated texts. (4) Distinct (D-n): It measure the diversity using the percentage of distinct n-grams to all n-grams in generated texts.
We follow to train a learnable metric to evaluate moral faithfulness. Specifically, we fine-tune RoBERTa BASE as a classifier to distinguish whether a story matches a moral.

We conducted a Likert-scale based manual evaluation... we require three annotators to rate its quality along with the input using a binary score in three following aspects: (1) linguistic fluency... (2) coherence... (3) moral faithfulness.

For each text we require three annotators to rate its quality along with the input using a binary score in three following aspects: (1) linguistic fluency: correctness in grammaticality; (2) coherence: reasonable relations between sentences regarding relatedness, causality and temporal orders; and (3) moral faithfulness: exhibition of a faithful moral to the input.
guideline: rate its quality along with the input using a binary score in three aspects
Annotators were asked to rate each generated text on fluency, coherence, and moral faithfulness using binary scores.
Three aspects are independently evaluated. We decided the final score of a text through majority voting.
